title: Registering a device with an API key
claim: With no pairing, the owner sets the name and bin first and copies the key onto the device by hand. Only a device added this way can be given a new key; a paired device gets one by pairing again.

nodes.desc: old key revoked, new hash stored

nodes.title: No button: pair the device again to replace its key.

steps: The owner chooses Register with API key, then gives the device a name and picks or creates a bin.
In one transaction the API adds the device with `registration = 'manual'` and no MAC, puts it in the bin and issues a key. The database only accepts `manual` when the MAC is empty.
The key is shown once on the page, with the address to send readings to. The owner copies it onto the device; readings are accepted at once because the bin is already set.

steps.text: A new key is checked three times: the Settings tab only offers the button for a `manual` device, the API refuses anything else with 409, and the database column the API checks is tied to the device having no MAC. A new key revokes the old one straight away.

notes: The two ways in are kept separate on purpose. Pairing proves the device holds the code; registration trusts the owner to put the key where it belongs.
The emulator cannot take a key by hand, so this path is tested with `emulator/tools/compostiq_test_device.py`.
